main_text.p: II. Sed constabit vis argumenti inductione exemplorum in actu exercito; & ad oculum demonstrandum quaenam sint, illa δυσνόητα[?], quae crucem figant, quaeque imperiti & male sani contorqueant. Et, quidem primo notari possunt illa de apostatarum interitu, Hebr. vi. & x. Quae quidem adeo perplexa ut I. Latini veteres Epistolam hoc fere nomine expungendam è Canonicarum censu, & nodum hunc secandum hac ratione censuerint.
II. Ut Novatus & Novatiani spem omnem, si non salutis, saltem veniæ in foro externo Ecclesiæ, post Baptismum in peccata prolapsis interdixerint.
III. Ut Clinici Baptismum nonnisi ἐπὶ κλίνης[?] & animam agentes susciperent, quibus dum se Patres opponunt, urgent necessitatem Sacramenti absolutam & medij.
IV. Ut Pelagij nepotes, apostasiam sanctorum to-talem finalemque propugnarint.
V. Ut iidem Christi mortem universalem etiam pro impiis & apostatis ex utroque loco defenderint.
VI. ut Romanenses hinc etiam suum pœnitentiæ Sacramentum & satisf[?]

page.notes: The page number at the top left is in an ornate form and is read as 98 with doubt. The running head is set in decorative type. The Greek word in item II (δυσνόητα) is partly struck through and is uncertain. The Greek in item III (ἐπὶ κλίνης) is uncertain. The numeral of the second item is printed "II." and would be expected to read "III."; the printed form is kept. The last line is cut off at the foot of the scan, so only "satisf" is legible. The word "secandum" is copied as printed. Ink spots and specks at the foot are not printed text and are left out.
